clue.text: Problem with vision producing fall

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clouding of the eye's lens

explanation.surface: Someone's poor eyesight leads them to take a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an eye condition that blurs sight and a great cascade of water.

clue.text: Not supporting, initially, art nouveau, that is

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: the first letters of art, nouveau, that and is

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are no fan of Art Nouveau.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something is the same as not backing it, so the preposition fits.

clue.text: Decidedly 2-D

parts.note: a deuce is a two in cards or dice

explanation.surface: A terse note that something is definitely two-dimensional.
explanation.walkthrough: '2-D' looks like an abbreviation for two-dimensional, but it is read as two pieces: the number and the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old-fashioned intensifier, 'deuced awkward' means extremely or decidedly awkward.

clue.text: Barely suppress emotion as second person working on sculpture

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
one who shapes material into a mould or form

explanation.surface: A sculptor's assistant struggles to keep their feelings in check.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn without flame is the image: feelings that simmer, kept just below the surface.

clue.text: Showing one's work, on the way out without greeting head of Bauhaus

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the others
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An artist leaving the Bauhaus school shows their work without saying hello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: the word for leaving goes around the greeting plus B.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists exhibit when they put their work on public display in a gallery.

clue.text: Fraction of number that's small, as may be expected

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
slang short for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A maths remark that a portion of some quantity is predictably tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks arithmetical, but it means a song: a snatch is a brief bit of a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a short fragment, as in hearing a snatch of a song or musical piece.

clue.text: As house decorators, they are tied to secure craft

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tradespeople who paint homes

definitions.text: they are tied to secure craft
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ropes at a boat's bow used to moor it

explanation.surface: Decorators who are bound to their craft, as if tradition held them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as a trade or skill, but here it is a boat; a painter is a mooring rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorators who paint walls and the bow ropes that moor small boats share this one word.

clue.text: Kind of date in store — belly's out of shape

definitions.note: the answer is a modifier, used before 'date'

indicators.note: something out of shape has lost its proper form, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A shopper who has bought too many snacks past their date gets a flabby stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops mark perishable goods with the last day they may be sold, the sell-by date.

clue.text: China admits team combining work of various artists

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a team of eleven, Roman numeral XI

explanation.surface: China lets in a squad that brings together artworks from many hands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ming is the dynasty whose porcelain gives its name to fine china; XI is eleven, the size of a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A DJ's mix or a compilation blends tracks by several performers, so blending such work is this.

clue.text: Distribute aid around half of El Salvador among picture-makers

definitions.note: a forename leading to the painter's surname

indicators.note: distributing spreads things around, so the letters are rearranged
around means one piece encloses the other
half of a two-letter word is just one of its letters

parts.note: the second of the two letters

explanation.surface: A call to distribute aid around El Salvador, with artists among the helpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'El Salvador' looks like the country, but it splits: El is wordplay and Salvador starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador is the first name of the Spanish surrealist, so his surname is the painter meant.

clue.text: With angry look one cuts prices for Matisse and others

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word goes inside it

parts.note: to lour is to scowl or frown

explanation.surface: A cross-faced dealer slashes prices on works by Matisse and his circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Matisse and his Fauve peers are known as painters whose work is driven by bold use of colour.

clue.text: Was in charge, we hear, so naturally dropped water supply

indicators.note: we hear says the word is chosen for its sound when spoken

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of things saw to it that water was provided.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation from clouds is the natural way the sky supplies water to the ground.

clue.text: Start-up without a prayer, mostly producing kind of ice cream

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top
without in its old sense of outside, so one piece encloses the other
mostly means most of the word, losing its end

parts.note: a form of prayer with responses

explanation.surface: A start-up company with no hope makes ice cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start-up' looks like a new company, but splits into a word for begin and a sign to reverse it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan ice cream comes in three striped flavours, named after Naples.

clue.text: Artistic problem that can force closure of play

definitions.meaning: first meaning: poor illumination for a painter

definitions.text: that can force closure of play
definitions.meaning: second meaning: dimness that stops a cricket match

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a theatre production being shut down, but it is a cricket match halted by umpires when it gets too dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters need good illumination, and in cricket umpires suspend the game when it is too dim to see the ball.

clue.text: Attributes the following solution mistakenly

indicators.note: something done mistakenly is put in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to the next clue, 17 across

explanation.surface: Someone credits the next answer to the wrong cause.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder comes from another entry: the next across answer in clue order supplies the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Attributes as a noun means characteristics or qualities, which is the plural answer.

clue.text: Point about film part neither section of Hollywood can get over

definitions.text: neither section of Hollywood can get over

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a prong or point of a fork or antler
a reel is a section of film

explanation.surface: A sharp remark about a film role that nobody in Hollywood can get past.
explanation.walkthrough: Hollywood splits into holly and wood, both trees: neither can grow beyond the altitude limit on a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the altitude or latitude beyond which trees, holly and wood among them, cannot grow.

clue.text: Skilled performer appearing in part I studied

indicators.note: appearing in says the word is found inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: running across part, I and studied

explanation.surface: An actor shows up in a role they had rehearsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides painters, the word names any performer of great skill, such as a musician or entertainer.

clue.text: It's raised among subjects daily

indicators.note: among means placed inside another word
raised in a down entry means lifted from bottom to top, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A topic keeps coming up among the matters discussed every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb, but it is a noun: a newspaper published every day, here the London paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily is a newspaper, and this is the long-established British national paper.

clue.text: Cricket side at Oval scored smoothly

parts.note: the leg side is half of a cricket field
an oval shape resembles the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricket team at the Oval ground made runs with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which hides that the word just gives the letter of its shape. The leg side is the half of the field behind a batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the musical direction written in a score for notes played smoothly and connected.

clue.text: Like star-cross'd lovers I enshrined in poetry

indicators.note: enshrined in means placed and kept inside something

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A poet places their own self within verse, like Shakespeare's tragic lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet, the 'star-cross'd lovers', live in Verona; the answer is also a Venetian painter, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's doomed couple came from Verona, so they are people of that Italian city.

clue.text: French illustrator upset editor, was abrasive

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Gustave Doré, the French engraver and book illustrator
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A French artist annoyed the editor by being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive' reads as rude in the surface, but the definition is literal: wore something away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a surface away gradually is what abrasion does, as wind and water wear rock.

clue.text: French master singer needs new arrangement

indicators.note: a new arrangement means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A French singing teacher says the song needs to be rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' suggests a music teacher, but an old master is a great painter: Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres is a celebrated painter of the French school, an old master.

clue.text: Still-life by Van Gogh one mounts

explanation.surface: A Van Gogh painting is hung on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounts' looks like framing a picture, but it just means goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Van Gogh painted several famous canvases of these purple flowers, both in the garden and in a vase.

clue.text: Another painter upset I'm goin' with Dali

indicators.note: something upset is knocked into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A painter storms off in a huff to spend time with Dali.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Modigliani was an Italian artist famed for elongated portraits, another painter in this themed puzzle.

clue.text: Youth, including one assigned position on ground

indicators.note: including means holding another piece inside

explanation.surface: A young player, one of them, is given a fielding spot on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid has been put down and set in place on a surface, like a carpet or brick.

clue.text: Detail of face Hals mishandled

indicators.note: something mishandled is botched and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Frans Hals, the Dutch portrait painter

explanation.surface: Frans Hals botched a small feature of a portrait's face.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelash is a small feature of the face, and the short form names it.

clue.text: Fauvist bringing a bright colour back, following fashion

indicators.note: following says one piece sits beside the other in sequence
back means the words are read from right to left

explanation.surface: A Fauve painter brings vivid hues back into style.
explanation.walkthrough: André Derain co-founded Fauvism with Matisse, the movement famed for wild, bright colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauvists were the early-1900s French painters using bold colour, and Derain was a leading one.

clue.text: Supervised some cricket followed by piece of play, we hear

indicators.note: followed by places the second piece straight after the first

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket

indicators.note: we hear says a word is chosen for how it sounds spoken

parts.note: a scene is a section of a play

explanation.surface: Someone watched over a bit of cricket and then part of a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is six deliveries bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work, so the past participle means supervised.
